To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the membrane domain of SBAT is organized in nine hydrophobic segments, H1-H9, with H3 and H9 forming long exoplasmal loops.
the human liver bile acid transporter has a topology with nine membrane-spanned or -associated segments.

(1) the human liver sodium-bile acid cotrans- porter (hNaBC1) has nine membrane-embedded segments, (2) the H3 and H7 sequences are exoplasmic and are not membrane-embedded segments and (3) the L256N mutant is inactive due to a lack of oligosaccharides and not due to a change in secondary structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of sodium-dependent bile acid transport in the liver.
the molecular structure of the human liver Na+/bile acid cotransported (hNTCP) and the molecular mechanisms involved in its function.
the identification of the membrane topology of the human liver bile acid transporter and the identification of the amino acid sequences that determine the membrane topology of this protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane topology of the SBAT is that of a seven-transmembrane domain protein with two amphipathic exoplasmic segments.
H3 and H9 are signal anchor sequences and the other segments (H1, H2, H4, H5, H6, and H7) are stop transfer sequences.
H1, H2, H4, H5, H6, H7, and H9 are transmembrane segments, whereas H3 and H9 are membrane-embedded but amphipathic segments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
H1, H2, H4, H5, H6, H7, and H9 are transmembrane regions and H3 and H6 are membrane associated.
the human liver sodium-dependent bile acid transporter has nine membrane-spanning segments.
H1-H9 are all transmembrane regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human liver sodium-dependent bile acid transporter has a unique topography that is different from the other members of the solute carrier 10 family.
the membrane topology of the liver bile acid cotransporter is different from the seven-transmembrane model of GPCRs.
the membrane topology of the liver sodium/bile salt cotransporter (NTCP) is not a simple seven-transmembrane model, but rather is a more complex model with a nine transmembrane topology.
